request: an under desk mount for my Mac Studio (2025)

body_sources.corner_r: no radius published on https://support.apple.com/en-us/122211; 0 is the enclosing box

attach.source: ISO 273 clearance hole for M4, fine 4.3, medium 4.5, coarse 4.8 mm (https://www.iso.org/standard/4183.html, sold; values as charted by https://mechcodex.com/reference/metric-clearance-hole-sizes). A 4 mm wood screw up into the desk; two at least, so the mount cannot turn about one, spread at least a quarter of the part across that face (our numbers)

followups.say: Apple's tech specs page says Height: 3.7 inches (9.5 cm), Width: 7.7 inches (19.7 cm), Depth: 7.7 inches (19.7 cm). It is https://support.apple.com/en-us/122211

attach.source: ISO 273 clearance hole for M4, fine 4.3, medium 4.5, coarse 4.8 mm (https://www.iso.org/standard/4183.html, sold; values as charted by https://mechcodex.com/reference/metric-clearance-hole-sizes). A 4 mm wood screw up into the desk; two at least, so the mount cannot turn about one, spread at least a quarter of the part across that face (our numbers)

why: The Mac Studio is not in stone's catalog, so stone must ask the person for its size and where the numbers come from, never guess them; the person answers with Apple's own rows from https://support.apple.com/en-us/122211. Right side up under the desk, front at -y. Apple lists 'On front (M4 Max): Two USB-C ports, SDXC card slot' (the M3 Ultra: two Thunderbolt 5 ports and the slot) with no positions, so the front stays open; the rear ports are listed with no location, so the rear stays open too, and the bottom is supported, not covered. The Mac has no screw points: the mount wraps the sides and top, bears on the bottom in three of its four quarters, and screws up into the desk through its top (attach +z). Load: the request names none, so the spec holds stone's 20 N default, as e07 does. Apple lists 6.1 pounds (2.74 kg, M4 Max) and 8.0 pounds (3.64 kg, M3 Ultra) on https://support.apple.com/en-us/122211, 26.9 N and 35.7 N, both above 20 N: this spec checks the path for a product given by the person, not the load a real Mac Studio puts on the mount (open: stone takes no weight yet).
